name: Neural Disruption Charge NDC-7 'Brainstorm'
description: The NDC-7 is an electromagnetic pulse device engineered specifically to target neural interface hardware rather than physical infrastructure, developed jointly by Zheng-Dao Bioelectric and Helix Biosystems under a defense contract that was quietly terminated after field trials produced unacceptable civilian casualty rates. The device detonates in two stages: an initial kinetic micro-burst clears a small physical radius, followed immediately by a precisely tuned electromagnetic pulse optimized for the frequency signatures of common neural interface chipsets. Operators with standard neural augmentation within 12 meters experience anything from temporary sensory disruption to catastrophic interface cascade — a condition colloquially called 'brainstorm,' in which the implant attempts to process the pulse as input data and floods the user's sensory cortex with recursive error signals.
manufacturer: ZHENG-DAO BIOELECTRIC / HELIX BIOSYSTEMS (joint, discontinued contract)
legality: Prohibited — classified as a neurological weapon under the GLMZ Augmentation Protection Statutes; possession is prosecuted as assault with intent regardless of deployment
specifications:
weight: 290g
diameter: 58mm
kinetic burst radius: 1.5m (fragmentation suppressed, structural disruption only)
emp radius: 12m primary effect, 20m degraded effect
target frequency range: Optimized for 2170–2195 neural interface chipsets (partial effect on older/newer models)
effect spectrum: Minor: sensory static, 30–90 seconds. Moderate: motor control disruption, nausea, 5–20 minutes. Severe: interface cascade, potential permanent damage. Fatal: documented in 7% of field trial subjects with high-integration implants
countermeasures: Faraday-shielded implant housing (rare, expensive), fully analog operators, pre-detonation interface shutdown
tactical_use: The NDC-7 is used to neutralize augmented security personnel, cyborg combatants, and neural-linked drone operators without destroying physical infrastructure. An operator with no neural implants — increasingly rare in GLMZ — can deploy a Brainstorm into a room full of augmented security and walk through the aftermath. Drone operations are particularly vulnerable: pilots whose neural links are disrupted lose simultaneous control of all linked units. The weapon is also used for targeted assassination of high-integration individuals, where the cascade effect produces deaths that superficially resemble implant malfunction.
cultural_context: The NDC-7 occupies a uniquely disturbing place in GLMZ's cultural consciousness. In a city where neural augmentation is near-universal among working professionals, a weapon that turns your own implants against you is existentially threatening in a way that conventional explosives are not. The Augmentation Protection Statutes were passed partly in response to early NDC field trial leaks. Among the unaugmented — the 'clean' communities in the outer districts who reject neural integration on religious or political grounds — the Brainstorm is sometimes spoken of with a complicated admiration: proof that augmentation is a vulnerability as much as an advantage.
known_users: Corporate intelligence units targeting augmented rivals
Pre-termination Zheng-Dao field test personnel (some gone rogue)
story_hooks: A series of 'implant malfunction' deaths among mid-level corporate executives is being investigated by a forensic technician who notices the cascade signature — someone is using NDC-7s and the medical examiner is being pressured to close the cases.
A clean operator is being hired specifically because the job requires walking through a Brainstorm deployment — but the operator starts to suspect they're the distraction, not the asset.

A Zheng-Dao Bioelectric whistleblower claims the NDC program wasn't discontinued — it was refined, and the new version targets a broader frequency range that covers 2195–2205 chipsets, meaning nearly everyone in GLMZ.

physical_description.visual_profile: A compact, ovoid charge device with an aggressive industrial aesthetic. The form factor suggests organized lethality—smooth curves interrupted by functional venting and sensor arrays. At rest, it resembles a scaled-up medical diagnostic pod crossed with a breaching charge. The device projects controlled menace rather than raw destructiveness.
physical_description.weight_description: Deceptively heavy for its size—290g creates substantial heft in the palm, suggesting dense internals. Balanced but not comfortable; designed for confident grip rather than prolonged handling.
physical_description.primary_material: Aerospace-grade composite shell with segmented titanium-reinforced polymer casing. Internal framework is precision-machined steel for electromagnetic shielding integrity.
physical_description.finish: Matte gunmetal gray with brushed titanium accents. The surface bears intentional micro-texturing to prevent slipping. Wear patterns show scuffing consistent with field deployment and hasty storage.
physical_description.color_scheme: Gunmetal gray primary with gunmetal titanium bands at equator and base. Accent: cold electric blue on sensor housings and frequency-tuning port.
physical_description.grip_texture: Rubberized polymer with aggressive grip texture—designed for gloved or augmented hands. The equatorial band is wrapped in thin textured steel mesh for enhanced purchase.
distinctive_features: Twin hemispherical sensor arrays (blue-tinted sapphire optics) positioned at north and south poles for frequency calibration
Micro-venting channels along the equatorial band to dissipate residual electromagnetic bleed
Small recessed tuning port (2cm diameter) marked with frequency calibration hash marks
Zheng-Dao and Helix Biosystems dual-stamp logos (partially removed/obscured on many examples)
Serial plate roughed and refinished, suggesting deliberate identification erasure on black-market units
Faint stress fractures around the equatorial band on well-used examples
Minimal indicator lights (red/amber, rarely visible) beneath the forward sensor pod
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: ZHENG-DAO BIOELECTRIC logo (faint) on upper hemisphere; HELIX BIOSYSTEMS stamped on lower base. Most field-recovered units have these markings partially filed or chemically etched away. Serial codes are present but often corrupted. Manufacturing date codes (2219-2221) indicate pre-termination production.
physical_description.condition_typical: Well-maintained examples are rare; most field units show battle-worn polymer with micro-cracking, faded lettering, and accumulated residue from electronic contamination. Storage damage (desiccation rings, corrosion bloom around sensor seals) is common. Military surplus stockpiles show orderly wear; black-market examples often bear jury-rigged repairs and aftermarket Faraday tape applied to critical surfaces.
